name: ECDH_helper
prose: Non-blocking ECDH step of libecc's example (curve_ecdh.c:81-228), called once for Alice and once for Bob; the shared state is the static buffers Alice_to_Bob and Bob_to_Alice and the static per-role private scalar and result (d_Alice/d_Bob, x_Alice/x_Bob). It returns -1 or a libecc error code after MUST_HAVE or EG checks when curve_name or role is NULL, the role is neither "Alice" nor "Bob" (an error message is printed for an unknown role), the curve name is too long (length including the NUL must be below 256), the curve parameters cannot be obtained or imported, or any later libecc call fails; these checks are performed by the code, not assumed by the caller. It initialises a projective point Q. If our public buffer is all zeros it generates a random private scalar d modulo the generator order, computes Q = d*G and exports it in affine form into our public buffer; otherwise it skips key generation. If the other party's buffer is still all zeros it returns 0 (nothing more to do yet). Then, if nn_check_initialized(d) returns non-zero, which the comment on lines 190-192 says means that the shared secret was already computed, it returns 1 without computing it. Otherwise it imports the peer's affine point, computes d * peer point, converts it to unique affine coordinates, prints "ECDH shared secret computed by <role>", initialises x and copies the first coordinate Q.X into it, prints x, sets the result to 1 and then (only on this fall-through path) uninitialises Q, x and d. Every early return and every error jumps to the err label, which skips that uninitialisation, so Q and the static d and x are not released on those paths.
note: curve_ecdh.c:81-228 read in full. Reviewer 1 right (the "already done" return 1 at 193-195 happens before the shared secret is computed in that call; it relies on d being uninitialised after an earlier completed call, which depends on libecc's nn_check_initialized semantics that I did not read); reviewer 2 right (the argument checks are in the code at 107, 138-148).

name: sha0
prose: Single-call SHA-0 helper of the libecc example (sha0.c:253-264). It declares a local sha0_context, calls sha0_init, then sha0_update with input and ilen, then sha0_final with output, and returns 0 on success. Each of sha0_init and sha0_update that returns non-zero makes it skip the remaining calls and return that code; the return value of sha0_final is returned as is. On success output holds the SHA-0 digest (SHA0_DIGEST_SIZE bytes) of the ilen bytes at input; on failure the contents of output are not specified by this function. It has no other side effects and keeps nothing beyond the call (the context is local).
note: sha0.c:249-264 read in full. The packet had marked it dropped as an unnamed wrapper; it is the function sha0 and is fixed under that name. The wrapper itself does not check input and output for NULL (any such check is inside the callees, which were not read).

name: shake256_final
prose: Finishes a SHAKE256 hash in libecc (shake256.c:41-54, compiled only when WITH_HASH_SHAKE256 is defined). First SHAKE256_HASH_CHECK_INITIALIZED(ctx, ret, err) checks the context (a NULL or not-initialised context, i.e. one whose magic is not SHAKE256_HASH_MAGIC, jumps to err with a non-zero ret, leaving the context and output untouched). Then it calls _shake_finalize on the context with output, which is where the digest (SHAKE256_DIGEST_SIZE bytes) is produced, and keeps its return value. After that call it sets ctx->magic to 0 unconditionally, whether _shake_finalize succeeded or not, so the context cannot be used again without a new shake256_init. It returns 0 on success or the error code of the check or of _shake_finalize; what output holds after a failure of _shake_finalize is determined by that function, not by this one.
note: shake256.c:41-54 read in full. Reviewer 1 right (magic is cleared even when _shake_finalize fails, line 50 is not guarded by EG); reviewer 2 right in that the digest writing happens inside _shake_finalize (not read), while only the magic reset is unconditional here.

name: _ecgdsa_verify_finalize
prose: Finishes an EC-GDSA signature verification in libecc (ecgdsa.c:500-613; the real name is _ecgdsa_verify_finalize). It first calls sig_verify_check_initialized(ctx) and ECGDSA_VERIFY_CHECK_INITIALIZED on the EC-GDSA data; a failing check jumps to the cleanup with that error. It zeroes the two local points, takes the generator G, public key Y, order q and the stored signature values r and s from the context, runs hash_mapping_callbacks_sanity_check, and finalises the hash with the hash function's finalize callback into e_buf. It converts the digest to an integer e (truncating by a right shift when the digest has more bits than q), zeroes e_buf, reduces e modulo q, and computes rinv = r^-1 mod q, u = rinv * e mod q, uG = u*G, v = rinv * s mod q, vY = v*Y, W' = uG + vY, converts W' to affine coordinates and sets r' = W'.x mod q. It compares r with r' using nn_cmp and returns 0 when they are equal and -1 when they differ. Any failing internal step (the hash finalisation, local_memset, nn_init_from_buf, the shift, nn_mod, nn_modinv, nn_mod_mul, prj_pt_mul, prj_pt_add, prj_pt_unique or the comparison itself) goes to the cleanup and its error code is returned. At the err label every path, success or failure, uninitialises e, r_prime, rinv, uv, uG and vY and, when ctx is non-NULL, zeroes the whole ctx->verify_data.ecgdsa structure (including its magic), so the verification context cannot be reused without a new initialisation; the local pointers are then nullified.
note: ecgdsa.c:500-613 read in full, comments skipped. Fixed under the real name; the packet's reviewer reason was the mechanical name rejection only.

name: _eckcdsa_verify_finalize
prose: Finishes an EC-KCDSA signature verification in libecc (eckcdsa.c:692-830; the real name is _eckcdsa_verify_finalize). It checks that the context is initialised (sig_verify_check_initialized and ECKCDSA_VERIFY_CHECK_INITIALIZED; a failure jumps to the cleanup with that error), zeroes the two local points, and takes G, Y, q, the signature part r (a byte string of length r_len derived from the digest size and the bit length of q) and s from the context. After the hash callbacks sanity check it finalises the message hash into hzm, drops the leading bytes beyond r_len (buf_lshift, with shift = hsize - r_len when hsize exceeds r_len; MUST_HAVE(hsize <= sizeof(hzm))), XORs the first r_len bytes with r, converts them to the integer tmp, zeroes hzm and sets e = tmp mod q. It computes sY = s*Y, eG = e*G and W' = sY + eG, converts W' to affine coordinates, exports its x coordinate into tmp_buf as p_len bytes, hashes that with a fresh hash context (init, update, finalize into r_prime), zeroes tmp_buf and the hash context, shifts r_prime the same way and compares its first r_len bytes with r using are_equal. It returns 0 when they are equal and -1 when they differ. Any failing internal helper (hash callbacks, hash steps, buf_lshift, the nn and point operations, fp_export_to_buf, local_memset, are_equal) goes to the cleanup and its error code is returned. At err, for every path, it uninitialises sY, eG, e and tmp and, when ctx is non-NULL, zeroes ctx->verify_data.eckcdsa (so the context is unusable without reinitialisation), and nullifies or zeroes the local pointers and scalars; the arrays hzm, tmp_buf and r_prime on the stack are cleared only on the success path (lines 764, 778, 785-786).
note: eckcdsa.c:692-830 read in full, comments skipped. Fixed under the real name; the packet's reviewer reason was the mechanical name rejection only. Note added: some stack buffers are not cleared on early error exits.

name: _ecrdsa_verify_finalize
prose: Finishes an EC-RDSA signature verification in libecc (ecrdsa.c:498-615; the real name is _ecrdsa_verify_finalize). It checks that the context is initialised (sig_verify_check_initialized and ECRDSA_VERIFY_CHECK_INITIALIZED; failure jumps to the cleanup with the error), zeroes the points uG and vY, takes G, Y, q, r and s from the context, zeroes h_buf for hsize bytes, runs the hash callbacks sanity check and finalises the message hash into h_buf. Unless USE_ISO14888_3_ECRDSA is defined it reverses the byte order of h_buf. It converts the digest to an integer h, zeroes h_buf, reduces h modulo q, replaces a zero value by 1 (nn_inc), and computes e = h^-1 mod q, u = e*s mod q and v = -(e*r) mod q. It computes uG = u*G, vY = v*Y and W' = uG + vY, converts W' to affine coordinates, sets r' = W'.x mod q and compares r with r' using nn_cmp, returning 0 when they are equal and -1 when they differ. Any failing internal step goes to the cleanup and its (negative) error code is returned. For every path through the err label it uninitialises h, r_prime, e, v, u, vY and uG and, when ctx is non-NULL, zeroes ctx->verify_data.ecrdsa including its magic, so the context cannot be finalised again; an error before the hash finalisation step leaves the hash unfinalised, and h_buf is cleared only after the hash was converted to h.
note: ecrdsa.c:498-615 read in full, comments skipped. Fixed under the real name; the packet's reviewer reason was the mechanical name rejection only.

name: _eddsa_sign_finalize_pre_hash
prose: Finishes a pre-hashed EdDSA signature (Ed25519ph or Ed448ph) in libecc (eddsa.c:1224-1551; the real name is _eddsa_sign_finalize_pre_hash and the packet name eddsa_sign_ph does not occur in the file). It checks that ctx is initialised and that sig is non-NULL (sig_sign_check_initialized, EDDSA_SIGN_CHECK_INITIALIZED, MUST_HAVE), clears its local buffers and points, and requires that the private and public key types match and that the hash mapping is the one for that key type. It computes the half-signature lengths r_len and s_len from the digest size and requires siglen == EDDSA_SIGLEN(hsize) == r_len + s_len; only key types EDDSA25519PH (pre-hash size hsize) and EDDSA448PH (pre-hash size 64) are accepted (any other key type fails MUST_HAVE). After the hash callbacks sanity check it finalises the message hash held in ctx into ph_hash (an error before this step leaves the hash unfinalised), derives the key hash from the private key (its size must equal hsize), restarts the hash with the domain separation prefix (dom2 or dom4 with the context data, pre-hash flag 1), feeds the second half of the key hash and the pre-hash (requiring use_message_pre_hash_hsize <= hsize), finalises it and decodes the result as the scalar r. It then multiplies the generator by r to get R (using random blinding of the scalar when compiled in, and an extra 1/4 factor for Ed448), converts R from the short Weierstrass to the Edwards form and encodes it into sig[0..r_len-1]. It then hashes dom2/dom4, the encoded R, the encoded public key and the pre-hash, finalises it, decodes and reduces the result as S, computes the secret scalar s from the key hash, forms S = (S*s + r) mod q (with blinding steps when compiled in) and encodes it into sig[r_len..siglen-1], requiring s_len <= siglen - r_len. It returns the status of the last step, 0 on success. On any failure it returns the failing step's error code and sig may be partly written. At the err label, on every path, it nullifies the local pointers, zeroes the scalars, uninitialises the points, curve and big numbers, zeroes ctx->sign_data.eddsa when ctx is non-NULL (so the signing context is unusable afterwards) and clears ph_hash.
note: Partly read: eddsa.c:1224-1551 read in full except the debug-print lines and the exact preprocessor conditions of the blinding code (lines marked #if were skipped, so which blinding variant is active in a given build is not stated); Edwards helper functions not read. Fixed under the real name; the packet's reviewer reason was the mechanical name rejection only.

name: main
prose: Command dispatcher of libecc's ec_utils tool (ec_utils.c:1592-1878). If argc < 2 it sets ret to -1, calls print_help(argv[0]) and returns. Otherwise it compares argv[1] (with are_str_equal; a negative error code from that call or from local_strlen is returned as is through EG) with the sub-commands, running every matching one in turn: gen_keys (argc must be 5; calls generate_and_export_key_pair with argv[2..4]; failure prints "gen_key error"), sign (argc 8 or 9; with 9 arguments argv[8] is taken as ancillary data whose length must be at most 0xffff, enforced by MUST_HAVE with no message; calls sign_bin_file; failure prints "sign error"), verify (argc 8 or 9, same ancillary data rule; calls verify_bin_file and prints "Signature check of <file> OK" or "failed"), struct_sign (argc 10 or 11; sign_bin_file with the metadata header type and version), struct_verify (argc 7 or 8; verify_bin_file without a separate signature file) and scalar_mult (argc 6; ec_scalar_mult). A wrong argument count prints "Bad args number" together with the argument list for that sub-command and returns -1 through the err label. If no sub-command matched it prints "Bad first argument" and the help text and returns -1. On success of the matched sub-command it returns 0. The return value of a failing sub-command is -1 (the callee's error code is not passed on). The function allocates nothing of its own.
note: ec_utils.c:1592-1878 read in full, comments skipped. Reviewer right: the check of the ancillary data length (MUST_HAVE at 1677, 1725, 1779, 1825) prints nothing before going to err; the old statement that a message is printed in that case was wrong.

name: sshpam_respond
prose: Keyboard-interactive response handler of OpenSSH's PAM module (auth-pam.c:984-1025); ctx is the struct pam_ctxt, num the number of responses and resp the response strings. It switches on ctxt->pam_done: a value of 1 sets sshpam_authenticated to 1 and returns 0 without sending anything; any value other than 0 or 1 returns -1; with 0 it continues. If num is not exactly 1 it logs an error and returns -1. It creates a buffer (fatal if allocation fails). If the authentication context is valid and either the user's uid is not 0 or options.permit_root_login is PERMIT_YES it puts the response *resp into the buffer; otherwise (invalid user, or uid 0 without PERMIT_YES) it puts a fake password derived from *resp (fake_password) into it, freeing the fake string afterwards. A failure to add to the buffer is fatal. It then sends the buffer as a PAM_AUTHTOK message on ctxt->pam_psock with ssh_msg_send; a send failure frees the buffer and returns -1, otherwise it frees the buffer and returns 1. The num check applies only when pam_done is 0.
note: auth-pam.c:983-1025 read in full, comments skipped. Reviewer 1 right (pam_done == 1 returns 0 and the num check only follows pam_done == 0); reviewer 2 right (the root-login restriction applies only for pw_uid == 0, 1008-1010).

name: userauth_finish
prose: Finishes one SSH user-authentication attempt in OpenSSH's server (auth2.c:360-464) and replies to the client; ssh carries the Authctxt, authenticated is the result of the method, packet_method its name and submethod an optional sub-method. If authenticated is non-zero it calls fatal() for an invalid user, for an attempt marked postponed, or for an unknown method name, and then uses the configured method name. If the user is root and auth_root_allowed denies that method, authenticated is set to 0 (with an audit event when SSH_AUDIT_EVENTS is built). If authenticated is still set and options.num_auth_methods is non-zero, auth2_update_methods_lists decides whether more methods are required; if so authenticated becomes 0 and partial becomes 1. It logs the attempt with auth_log and, when authenticated or partial, updates the session info. If authctxt->postponed is set it returns here without sending anything. With USE_PAM and an authenticated attempt it runs the PAM account check (mm_do_pam_account), sends any login message as a banner and waits for the packet to be written, and calls fatal() with "Access denied ... by PAM account configuration" if the check failed. If authenticated is exactly 1 it stops dispatching further userauth requests, sends SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_SUCCESS, sets authctxt->success and the log preamble (a send error is fatal). Otherwise it increments authctxt->failures only when the attempt is not partial, not a server-caused failure and not the first attempt with method "none"; if failures reach options.max_authtries it calls auth_maxtries_exceeded(ssh); then it sends SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_FAILURE with the list of methods that may continue and the partial flag (a send error is fatal). The function returns nothing.
note: auth2.c:360-464 read in full, comments skipped. Reviewer 1 right (failures not incremented for partial, server-caused or the initial "none" attempt, and the postponed return sends no failure packet, 406-407 and 444-446); reviewer 2 right (the PAM account check and banner and its fatal path precede the success packet, 409-429, and success is sent only when authenticated is still 1 after the root and multi-method checks).

name: channel_post_connecting
prose: Post-select handler (channels.c:2034-2104) for channels of type SSH_CHANNEL_CONNECTING and SSH_CHANNEL_RDYNAMIC_FINISH. It returns at once, leaving the channel unchanged, if SSH_CHAN_IO_SOCK_W is not set in c->io_ready, and calls fatal_f if the channel has no remote id. It reads the pending socket error with getsockopt(SO_ERROR) (a getsockopt failure sets err to errno and logs). If err is 0 it frees the connect context, sets the type to SSH_CHANNEL_OPEN, updates the used time and, unless the channel was an RDYNAMIC_FINISH one, sends SSH2_MSG_CHANNEL_OPEN_CONFIRMATION with the remote id, own id, local window and maximum packet size (a send error is fatal), then returns. If err is EINTR, EAGAIN or EINPROGRESS it returns without changing anything. Otherwise it logs the failure and calls connect_next on the connect context for the next address. If that returns -1 (no addresses left) it logs, frees the connect context and, for an RDYNAMIC_FINISH channel, calls rdynamic_close, or else sends SSH2_MSG_CHANNEL_OPEN_FAILURE with the remote id, SSH2_OPEN_CONNECT_FAILED and the strerror text (fatal on send error) and calls chan_mark_dead. In every case that reaches the end (a new socket or none) it then closes the old c->sock and sets c->sock, c->rfd and c->wfd to the value connect_next returned, which is -1 when the addresses were exhausted, and to the new socket otherwise.
note: channels.c:2034-2104 read in full, comments skipped. Reviewer 1 right (for RDYNAMIC_FINISH an exhausted list calls rdynamic_close, 2085-2086); reviewer 2 right (after the exhausted case the old socket is closed and sock, rfd and wfd are set to -1, 2102-2103).

name: channel_input_data
prose: Handler for an SSH2_MSG_CHANNEL_DATA packet (channels.c:3402-3468); it returns 0 in every path it returns from (errors are signalled by disconnect or fatal calls). It finds the channel from the channel id in the packet (channel_from_packet_id disconnects for an unknown id, not read). For a mux-proxy channel it forwards the packet upstream and returns. If the channel type is not SSH_CHANNEL_OPEN, RDYNAMIC_OPEN, RDYNAMIC_FINISH or X11_OPEN it returns without reading the rest of the packet. It reads the data as a direct string and requires the end of the packet (failure is fatal), and sets win_len to the data length plus 4 for datagram channels. If the output state is not CHAN_OUTPUT_OPEN it only reduces local_window by win_len and increases local_consumed by it, discarding the data, and returns. If win_len exceeds local_maxpacket it logs "rcvd big packet" and returns with no window accounting and no append. If win_len exceeds local_window it adds the excess to local_window_exceeded, logs, sets local_window to 0, and calls ssh_packet_disconnect if the accumulated excess is more than local_window_max / 10; otherwise it reduces local_window by win_len and resets local_window_exceeded to 0. In both of these last cases (when it did not disconnect) it appends the data to c->output, as a length-prefixed string for datagram channels, and an append failure is fatal.
note: channels.c:3402-3468 read in full, comments skipped. Reviewer 1 right (oversized packets return at 3440-3444 before any window accounting); reviewer 2 right (the data is appended after the window excess handling too, 3461-3465, unless the peer was disconnected).

name: cipher_init
prose: Creates and initialises a cipher context for OpenSSH (cipher.c:245-332). It sets *ccp to NULL and callocs a struct sshcipher_ctx (SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL if that fails). It records whether the cipher is "none" and the direction, and returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT if keylen is less than the cipher's key length or if iv is non-NULL and ivlen is less than the cipher's IV length. For chacha20-poly1305 it creates the chachapoly context from the key (a NULL result gives SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT); for the "none" cipher it succeeds with nothing further. Without OpenSSL, an AES-CTR cipher gets the key and IV set up directly (the iv pointer is passed to aesctr_ivsetup without a NULL check) and any other cipher gives SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT. With OpenSSL it allocates an EVP context (SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL on failure), initialises it with the cipher type and the iv pointer (which may be NULL here, but the AEAD branch below passes iv to EVP_CIPHER_CTX_ctrl with no NULL test), sets the GCM fixed IV for ciphers with an authentication length, adjusts the key length if it differs from the EVP default (EVP_CIPHER_CTX_set_key_length), and sets the key; each OpenSSL failure gives SSH_ERR_LIBCRYPTO_ERROR. On success (ret 0) it stores the context in *ccp for the caller to free with cipher_free; on any failure it frees the EVP context and zeroes and frees the partial context, leaving *ccp NULL.
note: cipher.c:245-332 read in full, comments skipped. Reviewer right: the "iv may be NULL" claim in the old precondition does not hold for the AES-CTR and GCM branches, which pass iv on without a NULL check (283, 301-302).

name: kex_assemble_names
prose: Builds the final algorithm list from the user's configured string (kex-names.c:242-336). Arguments: listp (the user's list, replaced by the result), the default list def and the list of all supported names all. It returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT if listp, def or all is NULL, leaving *listp unchanged. If *listp is NULL or the empty string it sets *listp to a strdup of def and returns 0 (SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL if strdup fails, in which case *listp has already been overwritten with NULL; an original non-NULL empty string is not freed). Otherwise it takes ownership of the old string and sets *listp to NULL. A leading '-' removes the named algorithms from def: *listp is set to match_filter_denylist(def, list + 1) (which may be an empty string), the old string is freed and it returns 0, or SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL if that returns NULL. A leading '+' appends the user's names to def and a leading '^' prepends them (kex_names_cat; allocation failure SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL); a list without a prefix is used as it is. For a '+', '^' or plain list it then splits a copy on commas; any pattern starting with '!' gives SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT; each other pattern is matched against all with match_filter_allowlist and the matches are concatenated in order into the result. An empty result gives SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT; otherwise *listp is set to the new string (caller frees) and it returns 0. After the initial argument check, every failure leaves *listp NULL, frees the original list, the working copies and the partial result, and returns SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL or SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT as stated above.
note: kex-names.c:242-336 read in full, comments skipped. Reviewer 1 right (after taking ownership *listp is NULL on failure and the original is freed); reviewer 2 wrong: allocation failures return SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL (263, 271, 280, 296, 308, 312), not SSH_ERR_INTERNAL_ERROR, and *listp is NULL on every failure after 259; reviewer 3 wrong: only a pattern that begins with '!' is rejected, the test is *cp == '!' (301). Duplicate removal, if any, happens inside kex_names_cat (not read).

name: kex_assemble_names
prose: This slice (kex-names.c:252-336) is the tail of kex_assemble_names (242-336); no function called kex_names_pick exists in the file. kex_assemble_names takes listp (the user's list, replaced by the result), def and all. It returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a NULL argument, sets *listp to a copy of def (0, or SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL) when *listp is NULL or empty, and otherwise takes ownership of the old list and sets *listp to NULL. A leading '-' returns match_filter_denylist(def, list + 1) (freeing the old list; SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL on NULL); a leading '+' joins def and the user's names with def first, a leading '^' joins them with the user's names first (kex_names_cat; allocation failure SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL), and a plain list is used as is. For these three cases the tail shown here splits a copy of the list on commas: a pattern beginning with '!' gives SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT; every other pattern is matched against all with match_filter_allowlist and the matches are concatenated, so the '+' and '^' lists are also filtered through all. An empty result gives SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT; otherwise *listp is set to the result (caller frees) and 0 is returned. On every failure after the initial argument check *listp is NULL and the original string, copies and partial result are freed.
note: kex-names.c:242-336 read in full. Reviewer right: the '^' case prepends the user's names before def (279) and the '+' and '^' results are subject to the allowlist filtering loop at 300-317; the old prose did not say so. The record's earlier name was wrong because the slice is the tail of kex_assemble_names.

name: kex_exchange_identification
prose: Exchanges the SSH protocol identification strings (kex.c:1234-1437; the slice cut the head). Our version buffer is ssh->kex->server_version for a server and client_version for a client, and the peer's is the other one; both are kept in the kex structure. It resets our buffer, treats an empty version_addendum as NULL, and formats "SSH-2.0-<version>[ <addendum>]\r\n" into it (a buffer error is returned with errno saved). It writes the whole banner to the connection output (a short write gives SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR), trims the trailing CRLF from our buffer, and duplicates it as a string (SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL on failure). It then reads the peer's lines. For each line, one byte at a time with an optional wait before each read when timeout_ms > 0 (a timeout sends an error message to the peer and returns SSH_ERR_CONN_TIMEOUT; another wait error gives SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR), a read failure with EPIPE gives SSH_ERR_CONN_CLOSED and other read failures SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR. CR sets a flag that the next character must be LF; a NUL, a character after CR other than LF, or a line longer than SSH_MAX_BANNER_LEN goes to the invalid-format exit; characters are stored in the peer's version buffer. A line of more than 4 characters starting with "SSH-" ends the loop; for another line, a server treats it as invalid, and a client discards it and reads the next, giving up after SSH_MAX_PRE_BANNER_LINES lines with an error message to the peer and SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT. It duplicates the peer string (fatal_f on failure), allocates a buffer for the remote version text, and parses "SSH-%d.%d-%[^\n]"; a parse failure sends "Invalid SSH identification string." and returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT. It calls compat_banner on the remote version, accepts major version 2 (and 1 only with minor 99), otherwise sends "Protocol major versions differ." and returns SSH_ERR_NO_PROTOCOL_VERSION. A server also returns SSH_ERR_CONN_CLOSED, after logging, when the compat flags mark the peer as a probe (SSH_BUG_PROBE) or scanner (SSH_BUG_SCANNER). On success it returns 0. In all cases the temporary strings are freed, and errno is restored when the result is SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR.
note: kex.c:1234-1437 read in full, debug and error log lines skipped. Reviewer 1 wrong: the peer's version is stored in the kex version buffer through peer_version (1244-1245 and the sshbuf_put_u8 at 1337), not in a purely local variable; reviewer 2 wrong: SSH_ERR_CONN_TIMEOUT is returned at 1304.

name: kex_ext_info_check_ver
prose: Static helper in kex.c (lines 410-424) that checks the version string of an SSH2_MSG_EXT_INFO extension. It returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT (after logging an error) if memchr finds a NUL byte within the first len bytes of val, leaving kex->flags unchanged. Otherwise it logs the value, compares val with want_ver using strcmp, and if they are equal sets the bit flag in kex->flags, else only logs that the extension version is unsupported; in both of those cases it returns 0. The strcmp reads val up to a terminating NUL, so val must be NUL-terminated (at val[len] or earlier, with no NUL before len, as checked). It allocates and frees nothing.
note: kex.c:410-424 read in full. Reviewers 1, 2 and 3 right: a NUL byte within len makes the function return SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT (414-417), so it does not always return 0, and the old precondition forbidding such a NUL was wrong.

name: libcrux_sha3_generic_keccak_absorb_full_9d_f8
prose: Generated (Eurydice/KaRaMeL) function for SHA-3 with rate 136 and one lane (libcrux_mlkem768_sha3.h:4588-4633) that absorbs all complete 136-byte blocks of the input slice inputs[0] into the Keccak state and returns the number of trailing input bytes that were not absorbed. It first calls fill_buffer_9d_b0(self, inputs), which, when self->buf_len > 0 and buf_len + input_len >= 136, copies 136 - buf_len input bytes into self->buf, sets buf_len to 136 and returns that count (otherwise it returns 0 and changes nothing). If that count is greater than 0 it loads self->buf as a block, runs keccakf1600 and sets buf_len to 0. With buf_len equal to 136 on entry the count is 0, so the buffered block is not flushed and buf_len stays 136. It then absorbs from the input, starting after the bytes already consumed, every full 136-byte block (load_block then keccakf1600 for each) and returns remainder = (input length - consumed) mod 136, which is between 0 and 135. It does not copy the remainder anywhere; self->buf_len is 0 after a flushed buffered block and unchanged otherwise.
note: libcrux_mlkem768_sha3.h:4554-4575 and 4588-4633 read; load_block and keccakf1600 not read. Reviewers right: with buf_len equal to 136 the fill step consumes 0 bytes and no flush happens (4561), and when no buffered block is completed buf_len stays as it was.

name: libcrux_sha3_generic_keccak_absorb_9d_7b
prose: Generated function (libcrux_mlkem768_sha3.h:4658-4682) for SHA-3 with rate 136 and one lane that absorbs a slice into a KeccakXofState and buffers any incomplete tail; it returns nothing and reports no error. It calls absorb_full_9d_f8(self, inputs), which first completes and permutes a buffered block when buf_len > 0 and enough input is present (setting buf_len to 0) and then absorbs every full 136-byte block of the remaining input, and returns the number of remaining tail bytes. If that remainder is greater than 0 it copies the last remainder bytes of inputs[0] into self->buf at offset buf_len through buf_len + remainder and increases buf_len by the remainder; with a remainder of 0 buf_len is left as absorb_full left it (0 after a flushed buffered block, otherwise unchanged). The copy assumes buf_len + remainder <= 136, which holds for buf_len below 136; with buf_len equal to 136 on entry the slice bounds are exceeded.
note: libcrux_mlkem768_sha3.h:4658-4682 read. Reviewer 1 right (when fill_buffer consumed a buffered block buf_len was reset to 0 before the remainder is appended, 4614 and 4680); reviewer 2 right (buf_len 136 is not flushed and the remainder copy would overflow the 136-byte buffer).

name: mm_answer_pwnamallow
prose: Privileged monitor's answer to the unprivileged child's getpwnam request (monitor.c:840-933). It calls fatal_f if authctxt->attempt was already non-zero (a second request), reads the user name as a cstring into authctxt->user (parse failure is fatal), and calls getpwnamallow(ssh, user). It sets the process title to "<user> [priv]" (or "unknown" when there is no entry) and clears the message buffer. If there is no allowed entry (pwent NULL) it puts a single byte 0 into the reply, sets authctxt->pw to fakepw() and leaves authctxt->valid unset; otherwise it sets authctxt->pw to the entry, valid to 1, and puts a byte 1, the uid and gid (and pw_change and pw_expire when the platform has them) and the strings name, "*", gecos and class (when present), dir and shell into the reply; any buffer error is fatal. It then sets the log preamble. If options.refuse_connection is set it logs "administratively prohibited connection" and calls cleanup_exit(EXIT_CONFIG_REFUSED), which ends the process. It appends the server options with mm_encode_server_options, calls auth2_setup_methods_lists (a failure is only logged at debug level), sends MONITOR_ANS_PWNAM with the reply, permits the monitor requests MONITOR_REQ_AUTHSERV and MONITOR_REQ_AUTH2_READ_BANNER (and MONITOR_REQ_PAM_START when USE_PAM and options.use_pam are set), and returns 0. MONITOR_REQ_PWNAM is not re-permitted here (it was entered with MON_ONCE).
note: monitor.c:838-933 read in full, comments skipped. Reviewer 1 mixed: on a failed getpwnam the reply holds only the byte 0 and valid stays unset, but the monitor's authctxt->pw is set to fakepw() (863), so both the old prose and the reviewer describe different sides of it; reviewer 2 right (no monitor_permit for MONITOR_REQ_PWNAM, 924-930).

name: mm_key_allowed
prose: Monitor wrapper in the unprivileged sshd process (monitor_wrap.c:498-540; the real name is mm_key_allowed, with type, user, host, key, pubkey_auth_attempt and authoptp parameters) that asks the privileged monitor whether a key is allowed. If authoptp is non-NULL it first sets *authoptp to NULL. It builds a request buffer with the key type, the user (or "" for NULL), the host (or ""), the key (sshkey_puts) and the pubkey_auth_attempt flag; any buffer error is fatal. It sends MONITOR_REQ_KEYALLOWED to pmonitor->m_recvfd and waits for MONITOR_ANS_KEYALLOWED (the receive helper checks the message type, not read), then reads a 32-bit allowed value from the answer. If allowed is non-zero and type is MM_USERKEY it also deserialises the key options with sshauthopt_deserialise; a parse or deserialise failure is fatal. It frees the buffer. If authoptp is non-NULL it stores the deserialised options in *authoptp (owned by the caller), otherwise they are freed. It returns the allowed value received from the monitor; *authoptp stays NULL when the key is refused or the type is not MM_USERKEY.
note: monitor_wrap.c:498-540 read in full. The packet name mm_sshkey_allow does not exist; the function is mm_key_allowed, and the old prose's description matches it (the old prose omitted pubkey_auth_attempt and the host/user substitution).

name: chan_send_eof2
prose: Static function in nchan.c (lines 183-204) that sends SSH2_MSG_CHANNEL_EOF for channel c. It logs a debug message and switches on c->istate. If the input state is CHAN_INPUT_WAIT_DRAIN it calls fatal_f when c->have_remote_id is not set, otherwise it builds and sends the packet carrying c->remote_id (a packet-building or sending error is fatal) and sets CHAN_EOF_SENT in c->flags. For any other input state it only logs "cannot send eof for istate" with an error message and changes nothing and sends nothing. It returns nothing.
note: nchan.c:183-204 read in full. Reviewers right: a state other than CHAN_INPUT_WAIT_DRAIN is not fatal, the default case at 199-202 only logs an error.

name: chan_send_close2
prose: Static function in nchan.c (lines 206-229) that sends SSH2_MSG_CHANNEL_CLOSE for channel c. If c->ostate is not CHAN_OUTPUT_CLOSED or c->istate is not CHAN_INPUT_CLOSED it only logs an error ("cannot send close for istate/ostate") and sends nothing. Otherwise, if CHAN_CLOSE_SENT is already set in c->flags it only logs "already sent close". In the remaining case it calls fatal_f if c->have_remote_id is not set (so the remote-id check applies only on this sending path), otherwise builds and sends the packet carrying c->remote_id (a packet error is fatal) and sets CHAN_CLOSE_SENT in c->flags. It returns nothing.
note: nchan.c:206-229 read in full. Reviewer 1 right (the missing-remote-id fatal is on the send path only, 219-220); reviewer 2 right (closed states not satisfied or CLOSE_SENT already set are only logged, not fatal).

name: process_config_line_depth
prose: Parses one ssh client configuration line (readconf.c:1135-2542; the real name of the function that contains this slice is process_config_line_depth, which process_config_line at 1125 wraps). This slice is a stretch of its big switch over the keyword opcode. The function returns 0 for an empty, blank or comment line and for a successfully parsed directive, and -1 (ret keeps its initial value) after logging an error for a missing argument, bad quoting, an unsupported or invalid value, an unimplemented opcode, extra trailing arguments, or other keyword-specific errors; some keywords instead call fatal. Keywords are lower-cased and looked up with parse_token; the rest of the line is split with argv_split and each case consumes its arguments with argv_next. For most options the value is stored only when *activep is true and the option is still unset (-1 or NULL), so the first value wins; IdentityFile and CertificateFile instead append to arrays when active (up to SSH_MAX_IDENTITY_FILES / SSH_MAX_CERTIFICATE_FILES, else an error); StreamLocalBindMask stores its value unconditionally, whenever it is parsed correctly (octal 0 to 0777), and not only when active and unset. Cases read in this part include time, flag, multistate and string options (via the shared parse_time, parse_flag, parse_multistate and parse_string labels), the key-file options and the known-hosts file arrays. After the switch, leftover arguments give the "extra arguments at end of line" error, otherwise ret is 0. At the out label it frees the canonical-name list, the string array and the split argument vector in every exit that reaches it.
note: Partly read: readconf.c:1133-1290 (head and the first cases), 1395-1452, 2294-2340 and 2495-2543 in full, and grep skeletons of the rest; the many other opcode cases (about 900 lines, including Host, Match, Include, forwards, SendEnv and the algorithm lists) were not read line by line. Reviewer 17 right (IdentityFile and similar arrays append when active, and StreamLocalBindMask is unconditional).

name: process_config_line_depth
prose: Same function as the other record (readconf.c:1135-2542), whose slice here is a later stretch of the switch. It returns 0 for an empty line, comment line or keyword-only line and for a successfully parsed directive; -1 (the initial ret) when a case jumps to out after logging an error (missing argument, bad quotes, bad or unsupported value, extra trailing arguments, unimplemented opcode, Host/Match/Include on the command line); for Include it passes on a non-zero return value; and some keywords (for example a missing channel timeout, PermitRemoteOpen, SetEnv or CanonicalDomains value, or an invalid argument for certain options) call fatal and do not return. activep NULL means a command-line directive, treated as always active, and depth is the Include nesting depth passed on to nested reads (read_config_file_depth, which itself calls fatal beyond depth 16). Most options are set only when active and still unset; the SendEnv and identity or certificate file lists append; StreamLocalBindMask stores its value unconditionally (readconf.c:2307). Host and Match can change *activep. On every exit that goes through the out label it frees the canonical-name list, the string array and the split argument vector.
note: Partly read (see the other record): the cases of this slice (about 2154-2407) were checked mostly through grep for fatal, case labels and StreamLocalBindMask; the Include, SendEnv and forward-related bodies were not read line by line. Reviewer right: StreamLocalBindMask is stored without the active/unset test (2294-2308).

name: main
prose: Entry point of the regress netcat (netcat.c:149-519); the function never returns, it ends with exit(). It ignores SIGPIPE and parses options with getopt; invalid options or combinations end through usage(1), errx(1, ...) or err(1, ...): no host or port, a single argument without -l (for non-unix families), -l together with -s, -p or -z, -k without -l, proxy (-x) with UDP, listen, unix sockets, IPv6 or -s, a bad number, and failure of mktemp for the temporary unix datagram socket. In listen mode it sets ret to 0; for AF_UNIX it binds or listens once, and for other families it calls local_listen on every loop iteration (a negative result ends with err(1, "local_listen")). With UDP and -k it calls readwrite(s); with UDP and no -k it peeks the first datagram with recvfrom, connects to its sender, optionally reports the connection and runs readwrite(s) (recvfrom and connect failures are fatal); for TCP it accepts one connection (failure is fatal), reports it with -v, runs readwrite on it and closes it. After each iteration it closes the listening socket for non-unix families (for AF_UNIX UDP it disconnects with connect(s, NULL, 0)) and, unless -k was given, stops. In AF_UNIX client mode it sets ret to 0, calls unix_connect and, if the socket is positive and -z is not given, runs readwrite and closes it; otherwise ret is 1 (with -z and a connected socket the descriptor is not closed); with -u it unlinks the temporary socket path and exits with ret directly. In the TCP/UDP client mode it builds the port list and for each port closes the previous socket if non-zero, connects directly or through socks_connect when a proxy is set, and skips ports that failed; for a successful connection it sets ret to 0, with -v or -z it runs the UDP test (a failed udptest sets ret to 1 and continues with the next port) and prints "Connection to ... succeeded!", and then runs fdpass (-F) or, unless -z, readwrite. After the loop it closes s if non-zero and calls exit(ret); ret keeps the value set by the last port that connected (or the earlier value if later connects failed), and the initial value 1 is used if no port connected.
note: netcat.c:296-519 read in full, comments skipped (the option-parsing loop at 171-296 was not read, so exact option letters are not listed). Reviewer 1 right (the AF_UNIX client path with -z leaves a connected socket open, 452-460); reviewer 2 right (a failed udptest after a successful connect sets ret to 1, 487-489, so "0 when the last connect succeeded" is not exact).

name: fuzz_next
prose: Advances OpenSSH's test fuzzer to its next variant (fuzz.c:283-378); it returns nothing and works on struct fuzz (seed, slen, fuzzed, strategies bitmask, current strategy, offsets o1 and o2). If fuzz->strategy is 0 or fuzz_strategy_done reports the current strategy finished, it callocs fuzz->fuzzed (slen bytes) when it is NULL and then selects the lowest strategy bit still set in fuzz->strategies as the new strategy, clears that bit and resets o1 and o2 to 0; if no strategy bit is left it returns at once, leaving the old strategy and offsets unchanged (so after the last strategy finished the old strategy stays selected and no new variant is produced). It then asserts that fuzz->fuzzed is non-NULL (an allocation failure ends there) and, depending on the strategy, copies the seed into fuzz->fuzzed and modifies it: FUZZ_1_BIT_FLIP flips bit o1 and increments o1; FUZZ_2_BIT_FLIP flips bits o1 and o2, increments o1 and, when o1 reaches slen*8, resets it to 0 and increments o2; FUZZ_1_BYTE_FLIP inverts byte o1 and increments o1; FUZZ_2_BYTE_FLIP inverts bytes o1 and o2 and advances o1 then o2 like the bit case; FUZZ_TRUNCATE_START and FUZZ_TRUNCATE_END copy the seed unchanged and increment o1 (the truncation itself is applied by fuzz_len and fuzz_ptr); FUZZ_BASE64 replaces byte o1 with the base64 character at index o2 and advances o2, then o1 when o2 wraps. The offsets are checked with asserts. An unknown strategy value calls abort() (also in fuzz_strategy_done).
note: fuzz.c:260-378 read in full, with the helper fuzz_len and fuzz_ptr at 397-437 skimmed, comments skipped. Reviewer 1 right (when no strategy remains the function returns with the old strategy kept, 307-309); reviewer 2 mixed: unknown strategies end in abort() (371-372), while the asserts only cover offsets and the fuzzed pointer, and the base64 strategy advances o2 before o1 (365-369).

name: brace_expand
prose: Expands the shell-style brace alternatives of an scp source pattern (scp.c:953-1016, using find_brace, emit_expansion and brace_expand_one at 788-950). It sets *patternsp to NULL and *npatternsp to 0, strdups the pattern into a worklist array "active" (return -1 if strdup or the append fails). While the worklist is not empty it pops the last entry and calls brace_expand_one on it, which looks for a brace group with find_brace and, if one is found, emits one new string per comma-separated alternative into the worklist through emit_expansion. A return of -1 from brace_expand_one (an allocation failure, or an empty or INT_MAX-or-longer pattern rejected by emit_expansion at 847-848) frees the popped string and ends with -1. If the pattern is syntactically invalid (unbalanced braces or brackets) it calls fatal_f and does not return. If the entry was expanded it is freed and the loop continues with the new entries. Otherwise it keeps only the part of the string after its last '/' (the whole string when there is no '/'), appends a copy to the "done" array (a failed append frees the entry and ends with -1) and frees the entry. At the end it hands the done array and its length to the caller (*patternsp, *npatternsp), which must free the strings and the array, and returns 0. On every exit the remaining worklist entries, the worklist and any done array not handed over are freed, so on failure *patternsp is NULL and *npatternsp 0 (a string passed to a failing append inside emit_expansion is freed there).
note: scp.c:788-1016 read in full, comments skipped. Reviewer 1 right (an invalid pattern calls fatal_f, 978-979); reviewer 2 right (emit_expansion returns -1 for a zero-length or INT_MAX-or-longer pattern, 847-848, which brace_expand turns into -1). The old note that the failing append string may leak does not apply to emit_expansion (872-874 frees it).

name: match_cfg_line
prose: Evaluates the criteria of a Match line of sshd_config (servconf.c:1049-1271); acp and avp are the argument cursor over the tokens after "Match", full_line and line serve diagnostics, and ci is NULL for a syntax check or describes the connection under test. It starts with result 1 and counts attributes. For each token it duplicates the string. A token starting with '#' consumes all remaining arguments and ends the loop. The criterion "all" returns -1 after the error "'all' cannot be combined with other Match attributes" when it is not the first attribute or is followed by an argument that is non-empty and does not start with '#'; otherwise (also when followed by a '#' comment, which consumes the rest) it ends the loop with result 1. "invalid-user" sets result to 0 when ci is NULL or the user is not invalid. The criteria user, group, host, address, localaddress, localport, rdomain and version take their argument either from an attached "name=value" form or from the next token; a missing, empty or '#' argument gives the error "Missing Match criteria" and -1. In syntax-check mode (ci NULL) or in test mode when the needed field is absent, user, group, host, rdomain and localport set result to 0; address and localaddress first check the argument with addr_match_list(NULL, arg) and call fatal() if it is invalid, then set result 0; a connection field that is NULL outside test mode calls match_test_missing_fatal, which does not return. Otherwise user is matched with match_usergroup_pattern_list, group with match_cfg_line_group (-1 returns -1, 0 sets result 0), host with match_hostname, address and localaddress with addr_match_list (a result of -2 returns -1; 0 or -1 set result 0), localport by comparing the parsed port (an invalid port returns -1), rdomain with match_pattern_list and version against SSH_RELEASE. An unsupported attribute gives an error and -1. A mismatch only sets result to 0; the loop goes on to check the remaining attributes. After the loop, with no attributes at all it returns -1 ("One or more attributes required for Match"); otherwise it returns result, 1 only when every attribute matched. The duplicated attribute string is freed at out and at the end of each fully handled iteration, but the continue paths and the early return -1 for a comment-only line skip the free, leaking that copy.
note: servconf.c:1049-1271 read in full, comments skipped. Reviewer right: any token starting with '#' consumes all remaining arguments (1072-1075), not only after 'all', and when that token is the first one the function returns -1 at 1262-1264 without freeing attrib.

name: wait_until_can_do_something
prose: Static function of sshd's server loop (serverloop.c:144-252) that waits with ppoll until the connection or a channel is ready. It sets *conn_in_readyp and *conn_out_readyp to 0, initialises a timeout, calls channel_prepare_poll (which sets up the poll array and *npfd_activep, so the active count need not be set on entry), and calls fatal_f if *npfd_activep is then less than 2. It adds deadlines to the timeout: the rekey timeout when rekeying is configured and not in progress, the unused-connection expiry (recomputed while channels are open or when it is 0, with the static unused_connection_expiry), the client-alive interval (starting last_client_time when it is 0), and 100 ms when a child has terminated and little data is waiting to be written. It sets entry 0 of the poll array to connection_in for reading and entry 1 to connection_out, polling for writing only when the packet layer has data to write, and calls ppoll with sigsetp. If ppoll returns -1 it clears the revents of all active entries and, for any errno except EINTR, calls fatal_f; on EINTR it returns with both ready flags 0. Otherwise it sets the two ready flags to whether revents of entries 0 and 1 are non-zero and re-reads the monotonic time. When client-alive probing is scheduled, a ppoll timeout (ret 0) with the interval elapsed calls client_alive_check(ssh) (which sends the probe and decides whether the client is considered dead; its body, including the client_alive_count_max test, was not read) and resets last_client_time, while activity on the input descriptor resets last_client_time. If the unused-connection expiry is set, has passed and no channel is still open it logs "terminating inactive connection" and calls cleanup_exit(255). The function returns nothing.
note: serverloop.c:143-252 read in full, comments skipped; client_alive_check not read. Reviewer 1 right (the active count is set by channel_prepare_poll, 162-165); reviewer 2 right in that the count-exceeded termination belongs to client_alive_check and depends on options.client_alive_count_max, not on this function.

name: sftp_download
prose: Downloads one remote file with SFTP (sftp-client.c:1596-1888) and returns 0 on success or -1 on failure; protocol errors detected while reading replies (unexpected message types, unknown request ids, oversized data) end in fatal and do not return. If attributes a are NULL it first calls sftp_stat on remote_path (failure: return -1). It derives the local mode from the permission attribute (0666 when absent), returns -1 if the permission attribute says the file is not a regular file, takes the size from the size attribute (0 when absent), opens the remote file with send_open (failure: -1) and the local file for writing, creating it and truncating it unless resume_flag or inplace_flag is set. A local open failure, a fstat failure when resuming, or a local file larger than the remote one when resuming closes the remote handle, frees it, closes the local descriptor if open and returns -1. When resuming it starts at the existing local size. It then runs a pipelined read loop: it queues read requests up to max_req outstanding, reads each reply and handles SSH2_FXP_STATUS (any status other than EOF sets read_error; either way no more requests are queued) and SSH2_FXP_DATA (written at the request's offset with lseek and atomicio; a write failure records write_errno and stops further requests; otherwise it updates maxack and the contiguous highwater mark; short reads are re-requested). An interrupt stops the queueing. After the loop it sets highwater to maxack when there was no read error, write error or interrupt. If inplace_flag, read_error, write_error or interrupted is set it truncates the local file to highwater (the highest contiguous acknowledged offset). With a read error it closes the remote handle and fails; with a write error it prints the error, closes the remote handle and fails; otherwise it closes the remote handle (a failed sftp_close or an interrupt makes the status SSH2_FX_FAILURE), applies the mode and the access and modification times when preserve_flag is set (failures only logged) and calls fsync when fsync_flag is set and the file was modified. It closes the local descriptor, frees the buffer and the handle and returns 0 only when the final status is SSH2_FX_OK, so every failure status, including SSH2_FX_FAILURE, is returned as -1.
note: sftp-client.c:1596-1888 read in full with debug and error log lines skipped. Reviewers wrong on the return value: the final line returns status == SSH2_FX_OK ? 0 : -1 (1887), so the SSH2_FX_FAILURE status becomes -1; reviewer 2 right that a sftp_close failure without any read or write error or interrupt does not cause the truncation (the ftruncate at 1831-1841 is conditioned on inplace_flag, read_error, write_error or interrupted).

name: srclimit_penalise
prose: Records a penalty against a client address in sshd's per-source penalty tables (srclimit.c:345-460); it returns nothing. It returns without changing anything when penalties are disabled (penalty_cfg.enabled false), when penalty_exempt is set and the address cannot be converted to text or matches the exempt list, when the penalty type is SRCLIMIT_PENALTY_NONE, when the masked address cannot be computed, or when the table for that address family is full and the overflow mode is DENY_ALL (it logs "penalty table full" and returns). An unknown penalty type calls fatal_f. Otherwise it picks the penalty seconds and reason from the type (crash, authfail, noauth, refuseconnection, grace exceeded), masks the address with the IPv4 or IPv6 mask length, and calls expire_penalties(now) before the full-table test, so expired entries may be removed even on the paths that then return. It allocates a new penalty with the masked address, expiry now plus the seconds and the reason. If no entry for that address exists, it inserts the new one in the by-address tree, marks it active when its seconds exceed penalty_min, inserts it in the by-expiry tree (a failure is fatal), logs it, increments the family's count and, when the count exceeds max_sources, calls srclimit_early_expire_penalties (permissive mode), then returns. If an entry already exists, it removes that entry from the by-expiry tree (a mismatch is fatal), adds the new seconds to its expiry, caps the remaining time at penalty_max, activates it if the remaining time exceeds penalty_min and it was inactive, replaces its reason, frees the new penalty and reinserts the existing one in the by-expiry tree (a failure is fatal).
note: srclimit.c:345-460 read in full, comments skipped. Reviewer right that the early no-op returns exist (358-367, 370-371, 396-397, 412-417); reviewer right that expire_penalties runs at 401 before the full-table return at 412-417, so tables can change even when the call is a no-op for the new penalty.

name: sshsk_load_resident
prose: Loads the resident (discoverable) security-key credentials from an SK provider (ssh-sk.c:801-892; the real function name is sshsk_load_resident, with provider_path, device, pin, and the output pointers srksp and nsrksp; the code is inside ENABLE_SK). If srksp or nsrksp is NULL it returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT before writing anything; otherwise it sets *srksp to NULL and *nsrksp to 0. It builds the provider options from device with make_options (failure: that error), opens the provider with sshsk_open (failure: SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT) and calls the provider's sk_load_resident_keys with the pin; a non-zero return is logged and converted with skerr_to_ssherr. It then walks the returned credentials and skips any whose application does not start with "ssh:" or whose algorithm is neither SSH_SK_ECDSA nor SSH_SK_ED25519. For each kept credential it sets flags to user-presence-required and resident-key (adding user-verification-required when the credential has it), builds a key with sshsk_key_from_response (failure: that error), allocates a resident-key structure that takes the key, allocates and copies the user id and appends the structure to a grown array (recallocarray); an allocation failure returns SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL. On success it stores the array in *srksp and its length in *nsrksp (NULL and 0 when no credential qualified) and returns 0. Every exit after the arguments check goes through the cleanup that frees the options, the provider handle, the provider's credential list, the pending key, the pending structure and the partly built array, so on failure *srksp stays NULL and *nsrksp 0 (set at the start). The caller frees the result with sshsk_free_resident_keys.
note: ssh-sk.c:801-892 read in full, comments skipped. The packet name sshsk_load_resident_keys does not exist as the function head, the definition is sshsk_load_resident at 801 (the earlier rejections for "name not in slice" were right). The old prose was mostly right but omitted the error from sshsk_key_from_response (850-852).

name: sshbuf_load_fd
prose: Reads a whole open descriptor into a new buffer (sshbuf-io.c:33-78); fd must be open for reading and blobp must be a writable pointer slot. It sets *blobp to NULL first. If fstat fails it returns SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR. When the descriptor is not a socket, character device or pipe and its reported size exceeds SSHBUF_SIZE_MAX it returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT. It allocates the buffer with sshbuf_new (failure: SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL) and loops reading 4096-byte chunks with atomicio until a read returns 0: if errno is EPIPE at that point the loop ends normally, otherwise the result is SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR. Each chunk is appended with sshbuf_put (its error is returned) and the loop returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT as soon as the buffer length exceeds SSHBUF_SIZE_MAX. After the loop, for a descriptor that is not a socket, character device or pipe, a reported size different from the number of bytes read gives SSH_ERR_FILE_CHANGED. On success it stores the buffer in *blobp and returns 0. On every failure after the buffer was allocated the buffer is freed, *blobp stays NULL, and the stack chunk is zeroed at the out label, which both the failure paths after the allocation and the success path reach; the two early returns before the allocation skip it. A read that ends at end-of-file normally relies on errno not being EPIPE; this was not checked against atomicio's implementation.
note: sshbuf-io.c:33-78 read in full, comments skipped; atomicio was not read. The old statement that SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT cannot occur matches the code since sshbuf_put gets valid arguments, but it was removed as unverified. The old prose said NO_BUFFER_SPACE comes from sshbuf_put, which is possible (the error is passed through at 58-59), and the invalid-format check also exists inside the loop at 60-63, which the old prose attributed only to fstat.

name: check_host_key
prose: Decides whether an SSH server host key is acceptable (sshconnect.c:966-1476; this slice 1334-1588 holds the end of this function and all of verify_host_key, which is the caller that passes RDRW and clobber_port 0). Returns 0 when the key is accepted and -1 when it is rejected; it also calls fatal in some cases and may recurse into itself. It returns 0 at once, after clearing UpdateHostkeys, when no_host_authentication_for_localhost is 1, the peer is local and no host_key_alias is set. A hostname containing special characters forces read-only mode; known-hosts files (user, system, and the optional hostfile command unless clobber_port) are loaded for the host and, when the key is not a certificate and check_host_ip is still set, for the IP address. For a key not allowed by HostkeyAlgorithms it goes to fail. The result of check_key_in_hostkeys on the host decides the case. HOST_OK accepts the key (a certificate is also checked with sshkey_cert_check_host and goes to fail if invalid), may disable UpdateHostkeys, may add a new IP entry to the user file and marks the key as trusted. HOST_NEW first retries once without the port (a nested call with ROQUIET) when a non-default port is used; if that accepts, it stops with the key accepted. Otherwise a read-only mode or a certificate goes to fail, strict checking set to yes fails, strict checking set to ask prompts the user and fails when the answer is not yes, and the key is then added to the user known-hosts file (an add failure is only logged). HOST_REVOKED fails under strict checking and otherwise continues into the unsafe path. HOST_CHANGED fails for certificates, for ROQUIET mode, and under strict checking; otherwise it falls into the unsafe path. The unsafe path disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication, agent, X11, port and tunnel forwarding and UpdateHostkeys, and calls fatal when ExitOnForwardFailure is set and any of those was cancelled. HOST_FOUND calls fatal. After the switch a check_host_ip mismatch (IP entry changed but host entry not) prompts under strict ask, fails under strict yes and only warns when strict checking is off. If the key was not trusted, UpdateHostkeys is disabled. The success path frees the strings and key lists and returns 0. The fail label, for a certificate whose status was not revoked, creates the plain key, drops the certificate and jumps back to retry with it; otherwise it frees everything and returns -1.
note: sshconnect.c:966-1476 read in full with log lines skipped; verify_host_key 1479-1590 read, it is a separate function not described here. The slice 1334-1588 starts inside this function, the old prose describes check_host_key correctly except that "after freeing all allocated resources" is not true for the paths that call fatal, and the possible recursive retry also exists for certificates at 1455-1466 and for the port retry at 1167. Not read: callee bodies (check_key_in_hostkeys, confirm, load_hostkeys).

name: load_identity_file
prose: Loads an identity's private key for client authentication (sshconnect2.c:1521-1598; the real name is load_identity_file, a static function taking an Identity). It returns NULL, logging "no such identity" at info or debug3 level, when stat of the identity file fails. Otherwise it loops over attempts i from 0 to options.number_of_password_prompts: attempt 0 uses an empty passphrase, later attempts read one from the user with read_passphrase and end the loop when that passphrase is empty. Each attempt calls sshkey_load_private_type. Success continues; a wrong-passphrase error sets quit in batch mode and otherwise just tries again; a system error with errno ENOENT sets quit, and any other error (including a system error with another errno) is logged and sets quit. If a key was loaded that is an authenticator-hosted key while options.sk_provider is NULL, the key is freed, the result is NULL and quit is set. When quit is not set it runs sshkey_check_rsa_length against options.required_rsa_size and on failure frees the key, sets the result to NULL and sets quit. If quit is not set, a key is present, the identity has no agent descriptor and is not an already-loaded private key, it calls maybe_add_key_to_agent. A typed passphrase is zeroed and freed (not the empty literal) and the comment is freed on each attempt; the loop ends when a key is loaded or quit is set. The function returns the loaded key (owned by the caller) or NULL when it fails, is refused, or runs out of attempts.
note: sshconnect2.c:1521-1598 read in full, comments skipped; sshkey_check_rsa_length, maybe_add_key_to_agent and read_passphrase bodies not read (including how the RSA check treats a NULL key after a wrong passphrase, 1580). The packet name load_private_key does not exist, the function is load_identity_file (1522). The old prose is mostly right; it called the ENOENT case a fatal load failure although it only sets quit and logs at debug level (1561-1564).

name: ssh_keysign
prose: Asks the external ssh-keysign helper to sign data for host-based authentication (sshconnect2.c:2011-2125; static function with ssh, key, sigp, lenp, data and datalen; the key argument is not used in the body I read). It sets *sigp to NULL and *lenp to 0 and returns -1 (logging the error) if _PATH_SSH_KEY_SIGN does not exist, fflush(stdout) fails, either pipe() fails or fork() fails; a failure of the second pipe or of fork leaves the already created pipe descriptors open (no closes on those paths). After a successful fork it installs SIG_DFL for SIGCHLD and keeps the old handler. The child side closes the unused pipe ends, dup2's the pipes onto stdout and stdin and the connection socket onto descriptor 3, closes higher descriptors and calls execl on the helper; a dup2 or exec failure calls fatal in the child, so the child never returns from this function. The parent closes its unused pipe ends, allocates a buffer (failure is fatal), puts the socket number (as 3) and the data, sends the request with ssh_msg_send (failure is fatal), reads the reply with ssh_msg_recv, closes both remaining descriptors, and on no reply logs and goes to fail without waiting for the child. Otherwise it waits for the child with waitpid (an error other than EINTR goes to fail), fails when the child did not exit normally or exited with a non-zero status, reads a version byte (failure goes to fail), fails if that byte is not 2, and reads the signature string into *sigp and *lenp (a parse failure goes to fail). At fail it restores the old SIGCHLD handler, frees the buffer and returns -1; on success it restores the handler, frees the buffer and returns 0 with a newly allocated signature the caller must free. The state of *sigp after a failed string read was not checked.
note: sshconnect2.c:2011-2125 read in full, comments skipped; ssh_msg_send, ssh_msg_recv and sshbuf_get_string bodies not read. Old prose claim of leaked pipe fds is right for pipe(from) and fork failures (2038-2045); the first return after fork-success restores SIGCHLD on every path after the fork in the parent, but the child never gets there.

name: process_gssapi_token
prose: Static function of the SSH client's GSSAPI authentication (sshconnect2.c:820-885) that processes one token received from the server and returns an OM_uint32 GSS status. It reads the Gssctxt from ssh->authctxt->methoddata and calls ssh_gssapi_init_ctx with options.gss_deleg_creds and recv_tok, which yields a status, an output token and context flags. If the output token has length greater than zero it sends one packet, SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_GSSAPI_ERRTOK when GSS_ERROR(status) is true and SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_GSSAPI_TOKEN otherwise (a packet error is fatal) and releases the token. When the status is exactly GSS_S_COMPLETE it sends, if the context flags lack GSS_C_INTEG_FLAG, an SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_GSSAPI_EXCHANGE_COMPLETE packet. Otherwise it allocates a buffer (failure is fatal), builds the MIC input with ssh_gssapi_buildmic from server_user, service, the string "gssapi-with-mic" and the session id, takes the mutable pointer (failure is fatal), signs it with ssh_gssapi_sign (this call overwrites status), sends SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_GSSAPI_MIC with the MIC when the new status is not an error (a send error is fatal), frees the buffer and releases the MIC. It returns the current status: the init_ctx status, or the signing status when signing was attempted. It does not free recv_tok.
note: sshconnect2.c:820-885 read in full, comments skipped. Old prose is right; qualified the "no free" claim to recv_tok only (it matches 884) and replaced "GSS_S_COMPLETE additionally" by "exactly GSS_S_COMPLETE" (848).

name: server_accept_loop
prose: Static function of sshd's listener (sshd.c:934-1294) that accepts connections and starts a session child. It first calls child_alloc itself (958) and allocates the startup poll index array and the poll array, so the caller does not need to have initialised the child pool. It then loops forever: with SIGHUP, SIGCHLD, SIGINFO, SIGTERM and SIGQUIT blocked it exits the process (closing the listen sockets and unlinking the pid file) with status 0 for SIGTERM and 255 for other termination signals when received_sigterm is set; reaps exited children on SIGCHLD; shows info; updates the process title when the active child count changed; and on SIGHUP closes the listening sockets once (lameduck) and calls sighup_restart when no listening startup is left. It builds a poll set from the listen sockets and the children's startup pipes (adding POLLOUT while a config or key buffer is pending) and calls ppoll with the old signal mask; a ppoll error other than EINTR is logged, EINVAL calls cleanup_exit(1), and any -1 result continues the loop. It writes pending config or key buffers to ready children (on a write error other than EINTR/EAGAIN it closes the child; when the config is fully sent it sets the keys buffer from pack_hostkeys), then reads one byte from each child's startup pipe (EOF or a read error closes the child, an early read while the config is still pending kills it, byte 0 on an early child marks it as no longer early, byte 1 on a non-early child closes it, anything else is logged). For each readable listen socket it accepts (an error continues the loop), clears non-blocking mode, creates the config socketpair and applies drop_connection (each failure closes the sockets and continues). In debug mode it closes the listening sockets, sets *sock_in and *sock_out to the new socket, sends the rexec state over config_s[0], closes config_s[0], frees the poll array and returns. Otherwise it registers a child, forks and in the child closes the startup pipes and the listening sockets, sets *sock_in and *sock_out, reinitialises logging, closes config_s[0], frees the poll array and returns. In the parent (also if fork failed, which is only logged) it closes config_s[1] and the accepted socket and reseeds the random generator (a failure of RAND_bytes is fatal). The only return statements in the function are the debug-mode one and the forked-child one; the parent leaves the loop only through exit, cleanup_exit, fatal or sighup_restart (whose body was not read).
note: sshd.c:934-1294 read in full, comments skipped, LIBWRAP section skimmed; sighup_restart, drop_connection, child_* helpers not read. Reviewer 2 right that child_alloc is called inside this function (958), so the old precondition that it must already be done is wrong; reviewer 1 right that the forked child returns normally (1257-1267).

name: sshkey_private_serialize_maxsign
prose: Serialises a private key and, for XMSS keys, advances the signature state (sshkey.c:3743-3770 with the WITH_XMSS definition; in the build without WITH_XMSS the definition at 3802-3807 ignores maxsign and printerror and just returns sshkey_private_serialize_opt with SSHKEY_SERIALIZE_DEFAULT). In the XMSS build, when maxsign is 0 or the plain type of the key is not KEY_XMSS it returns exactly what sshkey_private_serialize_opt(k, b, SSHKEY_SERIALIZE_DEFAULT) returns and does nothing else. Otherwise it runs, in order and stopping at the first non-zero result, sshkey_xmss_get_state, sshkey_private_serialize_opt with SSHKEY_SERIALIZE_STATE (the buffer receives the state before advancing) and sshkey_xmss_forward_state by maxsign. Whatever happened in those steps, including a failure of the first one, it then calls sshkey_xmss_update_state. It returns the first error from the three steps if any, and otherwise the error from sshkey_xmss_update_state, or 0 when everything succeeded. The update-state call is therefore also made after an earlier failure; its error is only returned when the earlier steps succeeded.
note: sshkey.c:3743-3828 read in full, comments skipped; the xmss helper bodies were not read. The old prose said update_state is called only when the earlier steps succeeded, which is wrong: it is called unconditionally at 3765 (the label out), and only its error is conditional on r being 0 (3766-3767); that was a reviewer claim confirmed by the code.
